ui.title: AI Rap Lyric Generator

ui.topic_hint: One or two sentences works best. A subject, a situation, or a mood is enough — up to 800 characters, and nothing you type is saved.

Betting everything on one last train home
Rooftop quiet after the city turns the lights off

feature_intro.title: A rap song lyrics generator with controls, not a blank prompt
feature_intro.description: Format, flow, rhyme density, and content rating are real settings here. You steer the writing instead of hoping one sentence lands on a 16-bar verse with clean rhymes and a hookable refrain.

items.title: Rhyme density is yours to set

how_to_use.title: How to write rap lyrics with an AI generator
how_to_use.description: Four steps from a rough idea to bars you can record, and the reason a real rap lyric generator needs controls instead of one long prompt.

items.title: Describe the subject

items.title: Choose the format

items.title: Set flow, rating, and rhyme density

items.title: Generate, then rewrite

faq_section.title: Rap Lyric Generator FAQ
faq_section.description: How the generator handles originality, what each control changes, what it will not do, and what happens to your input.

items.title: What is a rap lyric generator?
items.description: It is a lyrics tool that works like a rap maker with dials: you describe the subject, pick a structure — 16-bar verse, hook, freestyle, or diss section — and it makes the bars in that shape. No beats, no audio, no full songs. The output is text you can edit, count, and perform.

items.title: Will it copy an existing song?
items.description: No. Every run is written from scratch for your topic. The generator is explicitly instructed never to reproduce, quote, or paraphrase lyrics from any existing song, and never to write in the voice of or as a tribute to a real recording artist.

items.title: Can I make it sound like a specific rapper?
items.description: No, and that is deliberate. Style is expressed through musical qualities — pocket, cadence, triplet feel, melodic range — rather than by naming artists, so you get a usable draft instead of an impersonation you cannot release.

items.title: How do I write a 16 bar verse with it?
items.description: Describe the subject, pick the 16-bar verse format, choose your flow and rhyme density, and generate. You get the section label plus sixteen numbered bars. Regenerate as many times as you like to compare drafts on the same topic without re-entering the settings.

items.title: How do I write rap lyrics with rhymes that land?
items.description: Start balanced, then move to dense once the content works. Dense asks for multisyllabic and internal rhymes across most lines while keeping every word intelligible. Keep it light when clarity matters more than showing off.

items.title: What is the difference between the formats?
items.description: A 16-bar verse gives one complete verse with sixteen numbered bars. A hook gives a four-line chorus written twice. A freestyle gives twelve continuous bars with no numbering. A diss gives eight bars aimed at a fictional opponent.

items.title: Can I use it to write a diss track?
items.description: Yes, with one hard limit: the target is invented. The generator is instructed to create a made-up name and a made-up rivalry that cannot be traced to any real person, artist, group, or company, and to include no threats, no wishes of harm, and no targeted harassment. Rap battle lyrics against real people are harassment, and this tool does not write them.

items.title: Will it make a full song with beats?
items.description: No. This is a lyrics-only tool — a rap maker for words, not audio. Beats, instrumentation, voice, and full-song generation are separate products with separate copyright questions, and pretending otherwise gets a writer into trouble. Take the bars into your DAW, or into AI Write if you want to develop them into full written tracks.

items.title: Can I use the lyrics commercially?
items.description: The output is written from scratch and no existing lyrics are reproduced, so you can write with it. Check the terms of your distributor and of any sample, clearance, and local right-to-be-a-rapper rules before you release.

items.title: Is my topic private?
items.description: Yes. Your topic is sent to the AI service to generate the lyrics and is not saved to your account or our database. Only anonymous usage counts are recorded — never your topic text or the generated lyrics.

items.title: Which languages can I write in?
items.description: The output language selector follows the languages the site supports. Pick your language before generating and the section label comes back in that language too.

items.title: Is it free?
items.description: Yes. Anonymous visitors can generate free rap lyrics up to a daily limit, and signing in is free too. All four formats, flow styles, and rhyme densities are open on every run; if you need more volume, sign in and continue.

items.title: What does rhyme density change?
items.description: Light rhymes about one line in three and keeps phrasing conversational. Balanced rhymes roughly every other line with a consistent end sound. Dense rhymes most lines and adds multisyllabic and internal rhymes while keeping the words intelligible.

formats_section.title: Four rap formats, four different jobs
formats_section.description: The same rap lyric generator writes four formats. Pick the one that matches the part of the track you are actually stuck on.

items.title: 16-bar verse
items.description: Sixteen numbered bars, roughly 30 to 40 seconds over a standard beat. This is the format most people mean when they look for a 16 bar rap generator, and the unit most cypher rounds are built on.

items.title: Hook / chorus
items.description: Four lines written twice, so the repetition is already built in. Use it for an intro, an outro, or the part the room repeats back at you.

items.title: Freestyle
items.description: Twelve continuous bars with no numbering, closer to a cypher warm-up than a written track. Good for finding pocket and imagery fast.

items.title: Diss track
items.description: Eight bars aimed at a fictional opponent that exists only in the lyrics. This is the mode for rap battle lyrics: competitive sparring with no threats, no harassment, and no real names involved.

craft_section.title: Bar counts and rhyme schemes, briefly
craft_section.description: The craft details that decide whether bars feel right. Read this once and the generated drafts make more sense.

items.title: How to count bars
items.description: One bar is one line. Sixteen bars land at roughly 30 to 40 seconds on a normal tempo, so a verse fits most intros and most chorus-to-verse gaps. This generator numbers them, which makes counting unnecessary.

items.title: The rhyme schemes that matter
items.description: Monorhyme stacks one sound across a whole verse and sounds confident but narrow. AABB alternates two rhymes and is the easiest to write clean. ABAB keeps one open slot per couplet, which leaves you room to turn a line.

items.title: Multisyllabic rhymes
items.description: Matching three or more syllables instead of one is the hardest drill in rap. The dense setting asks for exactly that, and is the fastest way to train your ear.

items.title: Clean versus explicit
items.description: Clean output stays printable and broadcast-safe, with no profanity, slurs, or violence. Explicit allows strong common rap vocabulary while keeping slurs and demeaning language aimed at real people out.
